messages:
IncidentBot: ALERT: High 95th latency on /v1/generate (us-west-2) — latency spike > 1.2s, error rate 3.8%. Pager: oncall@redwood
Ryan: acked — I'm on-call. Pushing into the channel. Anyone oncall in us-west-ops? @Maya?
Maya: I'm here, seeing elevated CPU and OOMs on a subset of inference pods. Could be a vulnerable batch sizing change from the last deploy.
Alex: noticing high KV cache evictions and a flood of retries from our client library (10x) — looks like continuous batching exploded for a small path.
Ryan: ok plan: 1) scale up pool in us-west-2 by +20% (fast), 2) disable aggressive batching flag for the last deploy, 3) route non-critical traffic to us-east-1 fallback. I'll run steps 1+2 now.
Jenn: tagging runbook and starting incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1909504321 (temp). Adding stakeholders and customer list.
Ryan: scaling now — aws autoscaling group request +2 instances sent.
Maya: rolling restart of the problematic deploy in progress. command:
```
kubectl rollout restart deploy/inference-service -n prod-us-west
```
Alex: running query to check KV cache eviction rate:
```
curl -s 'https://metrics-api.internal/series?m=kv_evictions&region=us-west' | jq .
```
Maya: restart ack'd — seeing pods come up. error rate falling from 3.8% -> 0.4%.
IncidentBot: UPDATE: alert recovered for /v1/generate (us-west-2). Duration: ~18m. Incident severity: Sev2 (customer impact: elevated latencies for ~12k requests).
Ryan: temporary mitigation worked. We should still do a postmortem and calculate customer impact + SLA credits. Noting affected customers: 4 enterprise customers with reserved capacity + ~120 orgs on hosted plan.
Sara: scheduling postmortem — propose doc + 60m review tomorrow 10:00 PST. Who can lead? @Ryan?
Ryan: I'll run the postmortem. Please add timeline, root cause hypothesis, and hit list of actions.
Jenn: added MC table and initial timeline in the doc. Also attached logs and the deploy diff. Link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1909504321/doc
Alex: root cause: an unguarded change in dynamic batching heuristics from last push. Under a particular sequence-length distribution it increased per-batch memory and triggered OOMs on some older instance types, causing retries and cascading latency.
Maya: reproducer attached (small script) and PR that rolled the change: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/5423
Ryan: action items:
- A1 (Maya): revert dynamic-batching heuristic or add safe-guard + canary test — due 48h
- A2 (Alex): add KV cache eviction alert and dashboard — due 72h
- A3 (Jenn): notify top 4 enterprise customers and draft refresh message — due 24h
- A4 (Sara): schedule postmortem review + notify PMs/CSRs — due 24h
- A5 (Finance/Liz): estimate SLA credits and advise on billing flow — due 48h
Maya: started PR for revert, will mark as hotfix and tag for dedicated capacity instances.
Jenn: public status update draft:
"We've mitigated elevated latency caused by a batching change; root cause under investigation; postmortem scheduled; impacted customers will be contacted individually for credit review." Thoughts?
Sara: fine, keep it short. PMs will do deeper comms.
Liz: from finance: to estimate SLA credit we need: incident start/end, number of affected reserved customers, token/req counts per customer, contract SLA % and credit policy. I can do a preliminary estimate once Jenn posts timelines and impacted customer list.
Jenn: posted the affected customer list in the doc (redacted): 4 enterprise tenants (A,B,C,D) and aggregated hosted usage. Also attached per-tenant request counts for the window.
Liz: thanks. Preliminary calc: for enterprise reserved customers we typically prorate monthly commitment and apply up to X% credit for SLA breaches. For hosted customers on usage plan we issue pro-rata credit against last invoice. I'll run numbers and open FIN ticket.
Ryan: what's the expected timeline for issuing credits? Customers asking for timelines when we reach out.
Liz: typical internal SLA-credit flow:
1) Engineering confirms incident duration & scope (done by postmortem) — target 48h after PM review
2) Finance computes credit amounts and creates a credit memo — target 72h after step 1
3) CS/Account team approves messaging and issues credit to customer — target 96h after step 1
I'll try to compress but need approvals/GL entries.
Alex: can you confirm any downstream billing system limits? e.g., minimum credit size or batching multiple credits into one memo?
Liz: good point — for credits under $25 we usually aggregate monthly; for enterprise >$25 we can issue immediate credit memo. Also need to know if any customers consumed free-tier credits — that affects the offset account.
Jenn: I created FIN-4729 to track this: https://redwood.internal/finance/FIN-4729 (assigned to Liz). Added links to incident doc and logs.
Ryan: other follow-ups: update rollout gating to include canary load shapes similar to what triggered this. Add automated integration test to mimic sequence-length distribution.
Maya: agree. Adding integration test PR now.
Sara: calendared postmortem 10:00 PST tomorrow, invite sent to Eng, SRE, PMs, CS, Finance.
Liz: once I have numbers I'll post an estimated credit and required GL entries in FIN-4729. Jenn/CS: please prepare customer outreach templates — include exact credit amount and expected posting date.
Jenn: will draft customer emails after finance posts numbers.
Ryan: closing incident here — if anyone finds residual issues ping me. Thanks team for fast response. :tada:
IncidentBot: INCIDENT CLOSED (1909504321) — duration 28m from first alert to resolved state. Please triage and schedule follow-up tasks.
Liz: FIN update: I've started the credit calc, initial estimate ~$18,400 total across affected customers; enterprise credits roughly $12,600, hosted aggregated $5,800. Will confirm tomorrow in FIN-4729.
Jenn: noted — adding the credit estimate to the incident doc and flagging account owners. We should also loop in revenue ops for recognition impact.
Sara: QA/verification owner: Alex. Please confirm next week that the revert + alerts mitigated risk.
Alex: on it. I'll validate metrics and post results in the doc by EOD +2.
Liz: once final, I'll request GL entries and prepare the credit memos. Expect update in 48-72h.
